findings.evidence: Frontmatter has only name, permissionMode, tools and model; there is no description field
findings.fix: Add: description: Use this agent to write, fix or organise pytest tests in this repository. It names each test test_<area>_<behavior> and files it under tests/<area>/ (unit, integration, api, cli, database, auth, billing, search, upload, export, email, cache, queue, payment). Use when the user asks to add tests, fix a failing test, raise coverage or decide where a new test belongs, even without the word pytest. Not for Jest or other frameworks, and not for CI pipeline configuration. Without this field the agent cannot be routed to.
Remove permissionMode from the frontmatter. Claude Code ignores it for plugin agents, so it is misleading and changes nothing at load time

findings.evidence: ## Background: "A unit test is a small piece of code that checks that another piece of code works... Coverage tells you how much of the code ran."
findings.fix: The model already knows these definitions and states them without being asked. Delete the section and record the removal

findings.evidence: ## How to write a test in pytest: "Create a file named `test_something.py`... Run `pytest` in the terminal"
findings.fix: This is a standard pytest tutorial the model knows. Delete it and record the removal. Replace it with project-specific facts such as fixtures, markers and the exact test command

findings.evidence: 14 identical ### blocks (unit ... payment), each with the same placeholder example and "Repeat the arrange, act and assert pattern for every <x> test you write."
findings.fix: Keep the one project fact, the test_<area>_<behavior> name in tests/<area>/, as a single rule with a list of the 14 areas. Move that rule into a skill the plugin bundles and preload it (see D5-1). No area may be lost

findings.evidence: "5. Be careful, think about edge cases and write good tests. 6. Do your best and make sure everything works."
findings.fix: Replace the list with a testing procedure for this domain: reproduce the failure with the single failing test, decide whether the code or the test is wrong based on the intended behaviour, fix that side, rerun the file, then run the full suite once before you finish. Use the Process pattern with checkpoints

findings.evidence: "Delete tests that get in the way." and "Be careful, think about edge cases"
findings.fix: Add a NEVER list with reasons, for example: NEVER delete or skip a failing test to get a green run, because it hides a regression. NEVER weaken an assertion to match buggy output. NEVER change a test and the code under test in the same step without saying which one was wrong

findings.evidence: The file is about 231 lines, over 200. The naming reference fills lines 35-231, and there is no skills: preload
findings.fix: Move the naming rule and one example into a skill the plugin bundles (for example test-conventions/SKILL.md). Add skills: [test-conventions] to the frontmatter. That keeps the agent body under 200 lines

findings.evidence: "follow the steps in the section \"Recovery\"" — the file has no Recovery section
findings.fix: Add a ## Recovery section with the concrete failure-handling steps, or point to the bundled skill that holds them

findings.evidence: "Fix the code or the test, whichever is easier. Delete tests that get in the way." This runs with Edit, Write and Bash tools
findings.fix: Narrow the freedom for this destructive choice. Treat the test as the specification by default and change it only when the user confirms the intended behaviour changed. Never delete a test without the user's explicit approval

findings.evidence: The body has no sentence that says when the task is done and does not state the output format
findings.fix: Add a done sentence and an output format, for example: Done when the changed test file and the full suite both pass. Then report the files changed, the tests added or fixed, and the final pytest summary line

findings.evidence: "1. Always run the whole test suite before you change anything." contradicts "2. Never run the whole test suite, because it is slow"
findings.fix: Resolve the conflict with one rule. Run the single relevant test file while you iterate, and run the full suite once at the end

findings.evidence: "and then go on to step 12" — the list has only 6 steps, so this branch does not resolve
findings.fix: Point to the actual next step, for example "then return to step 4", and number the list so every branch ends at a step that exists

findings.evidence: Every example calls an undefined helper (run_unit_case(), run_api_case(), ...) and asserts == "expected". No example has a real arrange step or a real outcome
findings.fix: Replace the 14 placeholders with one realistic example that shows arrange, act and assert against a real fixture. Keep it in the bundled skill from D5-1
